content.title: Warriors Defeated By Lakers in Regular Season Home Finale
content.text: WARRIORS FACE CLIPPERS IN LA FOR FIRST PLAY-IN GAMEThe Warriors face the Clippers in the ninth vs. 10th-place Play-In Tournament matchup in Los Angeles on Wednesday. The Dubs went 1-3 against the Clippers this season, but in their win, they held Los Angeles to a season-low 79 points. The Clippers became the first team in NBA history to finish above .500 after once being as many as 15 games below .500 in the same season —they secured their 15th consecutive winning season. This Play-In Tournament game is a win-or-go-home duel between two of the most accomplished players of their era — Stephen Curry and Kawhi Leonard — who have each been the driving force of a championship team. “He’s [Curry] one of the greatest players to play this game,” Leonard said. “Even if it’s just a pickup game, just being able to share the floor with a player like that — being coached by Steve Kerr —also playing with Draymond, that unit over there is of championship pedigree. It’s a great opportunity. You can’t take it for granted.”LAST TIME OUTThe Warriors fell 115-110 to the Los Angeles Clippers in their regular-season finale on Sunday night at Intuit Dome. The Warriors finish the season as the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference and will face the Clippers on Wednesday night in Los Angeles in the SoFi Play-In Tournament. With his second basket of the game, Stephen Curry passed Jerry West for 25th on the NBA's all-time field goals made list. Curry played 29 minutes on Sunday night, his most since returning from a knee injury. Curry recorded 24 points and six rebounds on 7-for-14 shooting. »Full StoryVideo Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:59Remaining Time 1:59Highlights: Golden State Warriors vs. LA Clippers | 4/12/26INJURY & ROSTER NOTESGSW: Quinten Post (Right Foot; Injury Management), Jimmy Butler III (Right ACL; Surgery) and Moses Moody (Left Patellar Tendon; Surgery) are OUT. Team NotesLAC: Isaiah Jackson (Right Ankle; Sprain) is questionable. Bradley Beal (Left Hip; Fracture) and Yanic Konan Niederhauser (Right Lisfranc Ligament; Tear) are OUT. Team NotesCheck out the Betway Insider for NBA news, picks and opinions across the 2025-26 season.TWO KEYS:KEEPING UP OFFENSIVELYThe Clippers were 11th in offensive rating during the regular season (116.3 OFFRTG), while the Warriors were eight spots lower with a 113.8 offensive rating (19th). The Warriors averaged more points (114.6 PPG) than the Clippers (113.8 PPG), but should aim to narrow the efficiency gap to keep up with Los Angeles’ potent attack. The Clippers were one of three teams with a 60 true-shooting percentage or higher as the Kawhi Leonard-led offense (60.2 TS%) found itself in a group with Nikola Jokic’s Denver Nuggets (61.6 TS%) and Luka Doncic’s Los Angeles Lakers (60.9 TS%). Leonard averaged a career-high 27.9 points per game and did so on a career-best 62.9 true shooting percentage. Multi-time All-Star Darius Garland has added a different dimension to the Clippers' offense as an explosive guard who can create for himself and his teammates with distance shooting ability that he patterned after Stephen Curry. “It’s pretty cool going against a top-75 guy like that." Garland said of the matchup with Curry. "A first ballot Hall of Famer. It will be cool just to compete with a guy like that. The skill and the ability that he has — that affected me and the way that I play. It’s super cool to see that on the other end. It’s gonna be fun. Any time you play against top-75 guy like that or a first ballot Hall of Famer or someone that you’re inspired by or looked up to and watched when you’re growing up, it’s always super cool to go against him and go at him a little bit."Curry also shared his appreciate for Garland's game and the influence he had on it following the regular season finale in Los Angeles. “It’s surreal that you’re this deep into your career and you have that influence," Curry said. "He was a guy when he first showed up in Cleveland that you knew was gonna be a problem in the league just because of his skillset, his composure. Obviously his speed. He’s just a gamer. I know he’s been dealing with some injuries early in the year and over the course of his career. But when he’s out there he’s always a threat. It’s great to see him continue to grow and even in a new setting continuing to figure it out.”With Curry on the court, the Warriors have a 119.3 offensive rating and are 8.6 points per 100 possessions better than when he's off the court (110.7 OFFRTG). For context, their offensive rating with Curry slightly exceeds the Clippers' offense with Leonard (118.6 OFFRTG) but Los Angeles has faired better than Golden State when their All-Star is off the court (113.6 OFFRTG). DURABILITYThe Warriors enter the Play-In Tournament banged up. Stephen Curry has only played in four games since his return from a 27-game absence due to a runner’s knee injury. Curry has averaged 20.8 points in 26.8 minutes per game and has played in fewer than 30 minutes in every game. Front court veterans Kristaps Porzingis and Al Horford have been in and out of the lineup and only combined to share the floor with Curry once. And this doesn’t even include the other key contributors who suffered season-ending injuries — Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody. The Warriors will not only need their available veterans to be healthy throughout, they’ll also lean on them to play significant starting-caliber minutes. Play-In: The top six teams in each conference, ranked in order by win-loss records, qualify for the playoffs.
